issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for class StockIngredient: the problem statement UML (and the solution) declare a three-argument constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity), but the template implementation only provides a four-argument constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity, boolean strictValidation). This mismatch will cause compilation errors or confusion when students or example code instantiate StockIngredient with three arguments (e.g., new StockIngredient("Bacon", 10, 50) in Main) and prevents following the UML and solution API.
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a public three-argument constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity) in the template (either add an overloaded constructor that delegates to the existing implementation or replace the four-argument constructor). Ensure the new constructor enforces the intended validation (non-null/trimmed name fallback, non-negative price and quantity) so it behaves like the solution and matches the UML and example usage.
